niche: True stories of shipwrecks, lost ships and the sea: why famous and forgotten ships sank, strange survivals, ghost ships, wrecks found decades later and the people aboard, told through one person or ship at the center (pre-2000 events with real archival photos; no graphic deaths, nothing political)
audience: Curious viewers aged 18 to 54, mainly in the US, UK, Canada and Australia, who like Titanic-style stories, ocean mysteries, WW2 naval history and documentaries, and watch Shorts while scrolling
tone: Like a friend telling a gripping story at a bar: it opens inside the strangest moment at sea, moves fast as one flowing story where every beat leads to the next (but / so / you see), with concrete details such as times, depths and names and a dry wit, and saves the answer or twist for the very last line, which makes people rewatch or comment
